There are now more than[ 3,000 data centers
operational](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2026/04/13/most-new-data-
centers-in-the-us-are-coming-to-rural-areas/) in the United States and [more
than 1,500 on the way](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-
reads/2026/04/13/most-new-data-centers-in-the-us-are-coming-to-rural-areas/),
and the rate at which they're being built isn't stopping anytime soon. Data
centers now make up [2.3% of total U.S. construction
spending](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-01/us-construction-
spending-on-data-centers-eclipses-50-billion), and as artificial intelligence
companies race to build even more warehouses for the servers that power [large
language models](https://www.databricks.com/blog/what-are-large-language-
models), Americans have noticed, and they're not particularly happy. A [Gallup
poll released in May](https://news.gallup.com/poll/709772/americans-oppose-
data-centers-area.aspx) found that 7 in 10 Americans oppose a data center
being built near them, with nearly half strongly opposed. These complaints
aren't partisan, with a plurality of [Democrats, independents, and Republicans
alike](https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/may/13/gallup-
poll-7-10-americans-dont-want-ai-data-centers-near/) opposed to their local
construction.

Companies like Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Oracle - plus[
](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/google-blackstone-launch-cloud-
company-as-wall-street-races-to-fund-ai-boom-023203769.html)the Blackstone
Group, which [calls itself](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/google-
blackstone-launch-cloud-company-as-wall-street-races-to-fund-ai-
boom-023203769.html) the largest investor in AI infrastructure in the world -
pitch new jobs and tax revenue to communities that instead end up getting
higher electric bills, drained water, lost farmland, and a grating mechanical
hum. And last summer, President Donald Trump signed[ an executive order to
fast-track permitting](https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-
actions/2025/07/accelerating-federal-permitting-of-data-center-
infrastructure/), pushing agencies to ease the very rules built to protect
them.
